text: While Brown sat applauding himself, he heard horses on the road and recognized the voices of the minister and Deacon Gookin, who were also hurrying toward the meeting. <break time="0.8s" /> There is a goodly young woman to be taken into communion, said the deacon, and Brown, catching hold of a tree for support, nearly sank to the ground. <break time="0.8s" /> With heaven above and Faith below, I will yet stand firm against the devil, cried Brown, but a black mass of cloud was already sweeping across the sky and hiding the stars. <break time="0.8s" /> From the cloud came a confused murmur of voices, among which Brown seemed to hear the voices of pious townspeople and, at last, the sad voice of a young woman. <break time="0.8s" /> Faith, shouted Goodman Brown in a voice of agony and despair, and the echoes of the forest mocked him, crying Faith, Faith, as if bewildered wretches were seeking her through the wilderness. <break time="0.8s" /> Then something fluttered lightly down through the air and caught on the branch of a tree, and the young man seized it and beheld a pink ribbon. <break time="0.8s" /> My Faith is gone, cried he, there is no good on earth, and sin is but a name, and to thee, devil, is this world given. <break time="0.8s" /> Maddened with despair, Brown grasped his staff and rushed along the forest path, laughing loudly, until he became himself the most frightful figure in that dark wilderness. <break time="0.8s" /> At last he came to an open space, where a rock like an altar stood among four blazing pines, and a numerous congregation of townspeople had gathered in the red light.
